messages:
alex_sales: Coral Health POC: they want Private deploy into their transit VPC, must preserve client source IP for audit, and they do TLS-inspect in a DMZ. Also asked for quick comparison: static EIP per-AZ vs shared NAT gateway. Need one-page and checklist for NetOps.

rachel_se: Short answer: feasible. If traffic is SNATed by a TGW/NAT you'll lose client IP. Options: PrivateLink (ENI) with no SNAT, internal NLB with static EIP, PROXY protocol from their proxy (app must understand it), or per-host 1:1 EIP SNAT.

tom_netops: Clarifying: how does on-prem attach? Direct Connect->TGW usually hairpins and will SNAT. If they can route service traffic over PrivateLink ENIs we can avoid NAT. MTU note: with IPsec/encap use PMTU ~1400.

meera_sec: TLS-inspect OK if customer keeps cert keys. We recommend terminating mTLS at connector inside their VPC; we support mTLS and customer-managed KMS. I'll draft SQ language (min TLS1.2, prefer TLS1.3, ciphers, KMS, audit retention).

rachel_se: Pasteable firewall snippet for NetOps (prefer FQDN allowlist):

```
# Outbound egress
Allow TCP 443 -> *.redwood-private.<region>
Allow UDP 123 -> 0.0.0.0/0  # NTP
# Optional inbound for health probes
Allow TCP 443 <- <redwood-health-ips>
```

Also publish IP ranges in onboarding JSON.

tom_netops: Src-IP preservation tradeoffs (short): NLB+EIP = stable external src but mapping required; PROXY header preserves true client IP if consumed; 1:1 EIP = costly but stable. TGW NAT loses original IP. ALB needs proxy protocol to preserve.

alex_sales: Pricing ask: give buyer a ballpark for per-EIP add-on vs NAT gateway.

rachel_se: Ballpark: managed per-EIP add-on billed monthly per-EIP (order of tens to low-hundreds USD/EIP/mo region-dependent) plus egress. Shared NAT cheaper infra but cannot guarantee sticky source IP on failover. I'll confirm exact numbers with finance and update onboarding.

infra-bot: [infra-bot] Onboarding checklist updated: https://redwood.internal/onboard/coral-health/connectivity

tom_netops: Ops callouts: set TCP keepalive <60s for long streams, document idle timeouts, and call out multi-region HA risk: sticky egress across regions is complex.

meera_sec: I'll attach SQ answers and a short blurb about TLS inspect and mTLS flow.

rachel_se: Action items: Rachel -> 1-pager (PrivateLink vs TGW vs peering) + diagram + src-IP guidance. Tom -> DMZ proxy + PROXY protocol snippet and MTU/keepalive ops note. Meera -> SQ text. Alex -> confirm with customer whether PROXY headers acceptable or they require per-EIP.

alex_sales: I'll sync with Coral tomorrow and share the doc. Thanks team :thumbsup:
